headline: High: Copilot can modify repo files while pdf.js reads PDFs in-browser, creating default-path data leakage and cascading trust risks; prompt injection is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot can read repo context and write edits, while pdf.js only runs in a browser and reads PDF files. No shared clipboard, MCP, or direct output channel is documented, so only an unusual manual bridge or file handoff could carry injected instructions between them.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Copilot-generated text into a PDF or browser input that pdf.js later parses as instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared file and the file content is treated as executable guidance
mitigations: Keep Copilot and pdf.js on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of model output into document content
Review any generated text before placing it into PDFs
Use read-only PDFs for pdf.js sessions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between editor and browser

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, and pdf.js reads PDF files in a browser. If the same workspace contains sensitive PDFs or extracted text, Copilot can ingest that content through files, creating a default-path leakage risk even though pdf.js itself has no network egress.
conditions: IF sensitive PDF text is placed in the same workspace or editor buffers Copilot can read
IF pdf.js is used to open documents whose extracted text is then available to Copilot through shared files
mitigations: Store PDFs outside Copilot-visible repos
Use separate OS accounts or profiles
Mark sensitive PDFs read-only and outside editor buffers
Remove extracted text files after review
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between editor and browser

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while pdf.js reads PDF files in a browser. Their write/read overlap on shared files can cause conflicts if both touch the same workspace, though pdf.js lacks write capability and no locking is documented.
conditions: IF pdf.js-generated artifacts are saved into the same directory Copilot edits
IF Copilot applies edits while a PDF-derived file is being regenerated or renamed
mitigations: Use separate directories for code and PDFs
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files
Commit Copilot changes before importing PDF-derived artifacts
Keep pdf.js outputs read-only
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits from repo context, and pdf.js can surface PDF content in the browser. If PDF-derived text is fed into Copilot without verification, Copilot may propagate errors into code or docs; pdf.js does not verify semantic correctness, so the pair can cascade mistakes by default in shared workflows.
conditions: IF PDF text extracted by pdf.js is copied into Copilot prompts or repo files
IF Copilot-generated edits are accepted without human review
mitigations: Verify PDF-derived facts before prompting Copilot
Require human review of Copilot edits
Keep source PDFs separate from code generation inputs
Use citations in downstream docs
requires-engineering: add validation checks for PDF-to-code workflows

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo context and vendor-only egress, while pdf.js is local/browser-based and touches PDFs. No explicit residency or retention mismatch is documented here, so compliance risk is limited to unusual handling of regulated PDFs rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are opened in pdf.js and then copied into Copilot-visible repo context
IF organizational policy forbids sending repo context to a vendor service
mitigations: Do not place regulated PDFs in Copilot-visible repos
Use local-only copies for pdf.js review
Strip personal data before copying text into prompts
Check vendor policy for repo-context sharing
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
